trajectory_summary: This call never leaves the cost-objection loop the customer opened with in the first 20 seconds. The rep never runs the verify section, never asks why the customer is interested in solar, never captures a bill, and the call ends in a soft disengagement once the hard credit gate is confirmed. There is no evidence of a booked or tentative appointment, and no evidence of a graceful DQ handoff (e.g., roofing bridge, callback plan).
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear; the observed transcript supports a DQ read (credit below 670, no cash-offer follow-through) rather than any booked/tentative outcome — this should not be miscoded as a soft no_appointment without noting the hard gate that produced it.

observed_outcome.quote: No. I no. Only 6650 or something.
observed_outcome.reasoning: Customer states a credit score below the 670 threshold, which per qualifiers.credit_qualifier is a hard DQ; the cash-offer alternative is raised but never resolved, and the call ends with the customer disengaging rather than any appointment being set.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The call never reaches the bill_amount verify item — it stays stuck on cost/fee clarification and the credit qualifier before the customer disengages, so there is no bill figure to flip.

script_coverage.quote: This is Bucky with Ion. I'm reaching out about the solar form you filled online.
Do you have a credit score over 670?

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Repeating an unclear explanation instead of adapting language
primary_coaching_focus.quote: There's no cost at all. All you have to pay is just a cheaper monthly bill.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep repeats near-identical phrasing three separate times (00:48-01:58) while the customer visibly struggles to understand the financing concept, never rewording, slowing down, or checking comprehension. This is the single biggest driver of the call's breakdown and is directly coachable with a scripted plain-language alternative.

key_moments.quote: I just have a few questions to get started. Is that okay?
key_moments.stewart_read: The intro at 00:06 references the solar form but gives no state, no credibility anchor, and moves to the verify ask in 7 seconds flat — before the customer has even settled into the call. When the customer resists, the rep has no legitimacy foundation to fall back on.

key_moments.quote: So we have a bill swap program where we look at your power bill, and we remove it, and then we replace it with a lower and cheaper solar bill.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rather than redirecting the cost question to the closer, the rep launches into a full financial-mechanism explanation — closer-tier content — within the first 30 seconds, before any qualification has happened.

key_moments.quote: There's no cost at all. All you have to pay is just a cheaper monthly bill.
key_moments.stewart_read: This phrasing is internally contradictory ('no cost at all' / 'you pay a bill') and the rep repeats it three times without resolving the customer's confusion, suggesting the rep himself doesn't have a clean way to explain the financing structure.

key_moments.quote: Yes. This is for, like, people who qualify, and you I think you qualify.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep agrees with the customer's inaccurate 'grant' framing instead of correcting it or reframing around the customer's actual bill pain — a missed opportunity to pivot the conversation onto solid ground before the credit question lands.
